A total of 137 consecutive LARC patients from January 2019 to January 2022 were retrospectively included.

title: Association between follow-up endoscopic inflammation and subsequent esophageal stricture formation after caustic ingestion
creator: Yoo Kyoung Lim, Heejoon Jang, Ji Won Kim
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The prognostic accuracy of initial endoscopic findings using the Zargar classification for long-term outcomes remains imperfect. We evaluated whether mucosal inflammation on follow-up endoscopy provides additional prognostic information regarding the risk of esophageal stricture requiring therapeutic intervention. We included 20 patients with corrosive esophagitis who underwent initial endoscopy within 48 hours of caustic ingestion and follow-up endoscopy at Seoul Metropolitan Government Seoul National University Boramae Medical Center between January 1, 2010, and August 30, 2025.

title: Deep-learning-based survival prediction of patients with lower limb melanoma
creator: Jinrong Zhang, Hai Yu, Xinkai Zheng, Wai-kit Ming, Yau Sun Lak, Kong Ching Tom, Alice Lee, Hui Huang, Wenhui Chen, Jun Lyu, Liehua Deng
description: BackgroundFor the purpose to examine lower limb melanoma (LLM) and its long-term survival rate, we used data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results (SEER) database. To estimate the prognosis of LLM patients and assess its efficacy, we used a powerful deep learning and neural network approach called DeepSurv.

title: Systematic analysis of the Rboh gene family in seven gramineous plants and its roles in response to arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi in maize
creator: Fulang Wu, Manli Zhao, Yajing Zhang, Weina Si, Beijiu Cheng, Xiaoyu Li
description: BackgroundPlant respiratory burst oxidase homolog (Rboh) gene family produces reactive oxygen species (ROS), and it plays key roles in plant–microbe interaction. Most Rboh gene family-related studies mainly focused on dicotyledonous plants; however, little is known about the roles of Rboh genes in gramineae.

title: Low serum iPTH at the end of surgery is the earliest predictor of postoperative hypocalcemia after total thyroidectomy
creator: Alexandros Lalos, Alexander Wilhelm, Katja Linke, Stephanie Taha-Mehlitz, Beat Müller, Alberto Posabella, Beatrice Kern
description: BackgroundThe most frequent complication of total thyroidectomy remains hypocalcemia due to low postoperative levels of serum intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH). The purpose of this study was to investigate the role of decreased iPTH at the end of surgery in predicting hypocalcemia. In addition, we examined the percentage decrease of iPTH as potential indicator of hypocalcemia.

title: Association of different leisure-time physical activity patterns with risk of sarcopenia among US adults
creator: Linbo Peng, Kexin Wang, Mingke You, Bin Shen, Jian Li
description: Sarcopenia, a progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and function, poses significant challenges to healthy aging. While leisure-time physical activity (LTPA) has been associated with better muscle-related health, it remains unclear whether condensed activity patterns: such as the “weekend warrior” model: show associations comparable to those of regular activity routines. We analyzed data from 11,780 U.S.

title: Influenza vaccine: a review on current scenario and future prospects
creator: Dipanshi Gupta, Sumedha Mohan
description: Vaccination is a crucial tool in preventing influenza, but it requires annual updates in vaccine composition due to the ever-changing nature of the flu virus. While healthcare and economic burdens have reduced, the virus remains a challenge. Research conducted over the past decade has revealed pathways for improvement through both basic and clinical studies.

title: The effects of abaloparatide on hip geometry and biomechanical properties in Japanese osteoporotic patients assessed using DXA-based hip structural analysis: results of the Japanese phase 3 ACTIVE-J trial
creator: Teruki Sone, Kazuhiro Ohnaru, Takumi Sugai, Akiko Yamashita, Nobukazu Okimoto, Tetsuo Inoue, Toshio Matsumoto
description: SummaryDaily subcutaneous injection of 80 μg abaloparatide increased bone mineral density in Japanese patients with osteoporosis at high fracture risk in the ACTIVE-J trial. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry–based hip structural analysis from ACTIVE-J data showed improved hip geometry and biomechanical properties with abaloparatide compared with placebo.

title: RETRACTED ARTICLE: Advancing breast cancer diagnosis with a near-infrared fluorescence imaging smart sensor for estrogen/progesterone receptor detection
creator: Gong Zhang, Min Dong, Xiulei Yao, Yuke Xia, Han Yu, Yu zhou, Chao Lian, Yunlei Zhang, Yiyao Cui
description: Molecular-genetic imaging has greatly advanced clinical diagnosis and prognosis monitoring. However, the specific visualization of intracellular proteins such as estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR) remains an elusive goal. Here, we highlight a novel method for selectively detecting ER/PR positive tumors using genetically engineered responsive elements.

title: Semiconductivity induced by spin–orbit coupling in Pb9Cu(PO4)6O
creator: Hua Bai, Jianrong Ye, Lei Gao, Chunhua Zeng, Wuming Liu
description: Recently, a possible room-temperature superconductor known as LK-99 (Pb10-xCux(PO4)6O (0.9 < x < 1.1)) has sparked a wave of research. However, many experimental works have proven that it is a semiconductor. At the same time, many theoretical works have reached the conclusion that it is a flat band metal.

title: Gene interaction network analysis in multiple myeloma detects complex immune dysregulation associated with shorter survival
creator: Anish K Simhal, Kylee H Maclachlan, Rena Elkin, Jiening Zhu, Larry Norton, Joseph O Deasy, Jung Hun Oh, Saad Z Usmani, Allen Tannenbaum
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The plasma cell cancer multiple myeloma (MM) varies significantly in genomic characteristics, response to therapy, and long-term prognosis. To investigate global interactions in MM, we combined a known protein interaction network with a large clinically annotated MM dataset. We hypothesized that an unbiased network analysis method based on large-scale similarities in gene expression, copy number aberration, and protein interactions may provide novel biological insights.

title: Mediating roles of systemic immune-inflammation index and body mass index in the association between dietary inflammatory index and cardiovascular disease in diabetes
creator: Shaofang Tang, Hongtao Li, Zixun Wang, Baoping Wang, Zhiqing Li, Yin Li, Chenlin Dai
description: This study aimed to analyze the dietary inflammatory index (DII) and its impact on cardiovascular disease (CVD) in individuals with diabetes and to explore the role of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and body mass index (BMI) in the relationship between DII and CVD. Data were obtained from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2009 to 2023.

title: A causal relationship between chronic pancreatitis and cardiovascular disease
creator: Shien Shen, Yuenan Zhu, Jieqiong Lin, Liang Zhao, Xiaona Shao, Nuonan Yang, Yuning Huang, Ruiwei Shen, Jianwei Shen
description: Current research suggests a link between chronic pancreatitis (CP) and cardiovascular disease (CVD), although the causality remains unclear. The aim of this study was therefore to conduct a 2-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to determine whether a causal relationship exists between CP and CVD.

title: Psychological experiences of unplanned interruption of patient-controlled intravenous analgesia in adult postoperative patients
creator: Jiao Qin, Wei Zhang, Qiuyue Yang, Ling-yan Gou
description: This qualitative study aimed to explore the psychological experiences of adult postoperative patients who unplanned discontinued patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA), based on the stress and coping theory and the Activating event, Beliefs, Consequences emotion theory. The findings are intended to provide insights for developing individualized analgesia management and psychological interventions in clinical practice.

title: Phenotyping and unmet need assessment for biological agents in uncontrolled asthma
creator: Rahul Tyagi, Randeep Guleria, Pawan Tiwari, Karan Madan, Anant Mohan, Vijay Hadda, Ravindra Mohan Pandey, Saurabh Mittal
description: Setting:Uncontrolled asthma patients at a university teaching hospital in India.Objective:To determine the prevalence, endotypes, and need for add-on therapies in severe asthma.Methods:This prospective study screened all patients with uncontrolled asthma, and those with uncontrolled asthma while on moderate-to-high dose inhaled corticosteroids with long-acting beta agonists (ICS + LABA) were further assessed.

title: Beyond hysteroscopic metroplasty: time to distinguish fundal from ampliative procedures
creator: Ursula Catena, Attilio Di Spiezio Sardo, Grigoris Grimbizis
description: Functional intrauterine surgery has recently been proposed as a conceptual framework shifting the focus from anatomical correction alone toward restoration of uterine function and reproductive competence. However, hysteroscopic treatment of congenital uterine anomalies continues to be described under the umbrella term metroplasty, despite substantial differences in uterine morphology, surgical targets, and reconstructive objectives.

title: Human iPSC‐Derived Brain Organoids: A Disease‐Oriented Evaluation of Modeling Fidelity
creator: Bishwa R Pokharel, Abigail Dickerson, Sanjana G Shenoy, Mira S Ramasamy, Niska Majumdar, Paul P Cook, Shaw M Akula
description: Two‐dimensional (2D) cell culture systems and conventional animal models have been crucial in the study of central nervous system (CNS) pathology. However, they are limited in their abilities to elucidate human‐specific neurobiology and disease etiology. Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)‐derived brain organoids have emerged as a complementary platform that offers a three‐dimensional (3D) structure and human‐specific environment.

title: Clinical management of clonal hematopoiesis
creator: Kelly S. Chien, Guillermo Garcia‐Manero
description: Clonal hematopoiesis, particularly clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential and clonal cytopenia of undetermined significance, is an age‐related premalignant condition characterized by the expansion of hematopoietic clones carrying somatic mutations. Because of the accessibility of peripheral blood, it has been increasingly detected, even in otherwise healthy individuals.

title: Tenecteplase versus standard care for minor ischaemic stroke according to the baseline occlusion status in TEMPO-2 trial
creator: Silja Räty, Daniel Strbian, Nishita Singh, Shabnam Vatanpour, Liisa Tomppo, Aravind Ganesh, Bruce C V Campbell, Mark W Parsons, Michael D Hill, Shelagh B Coutts
description: IntroductionPatients with minor ischaemic stroke (NIHSS ≤ 5) and intracranial occlusion or focal perfusion abnormality ≤ 12 h of onset did not benefit from intravenous tenecteplase compared to non-thrombolytic standard care (control) in the Tenecteplase vs Standard of Care for Minor Ischaemic Stroke with Proven Occlusion (TEMPO-2) trial.

title: IRS: iterative reference selection improves normalization of microbiome sequencing data
creator: Yiming Shi, Lili Liu, Jun Chen, Kristine M Wylie, Todd N Wylie, Sung Hee Park, Ruiwen Zhou, Yin Cao, Stephanie A Fritz, Molly J Stout, Maria Cristina Vazquez Guillamet, Lei Liu
description: Microbiome studies often seek to determine how the absolute abundances of individual taxa change across biological conditions, yet sequencing read counts are sample-specific scaled representations of those abundances. Because sampling depth can differ across samples, fold changes calculated directly from sequencing read counts do not generally represent absolute-abundance fold changes.

title: Fragment-Based Discovery of KLK6 and KLK7 Inhibitors
creator: Renato Ferreira de Freitas, Feryel Soualmia, Rilès Boumali, Yasmine Harrak, Chahrazade El Amri
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Human tissue kallikreins are serine proteases implicated in the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases, skin disorders, and various cancers. Despite their therapeutic relevance, the development of selective small-molecule inhibitors for these enzymes has been limited compared to other serine proteases. To address this, we implemented a fragment-based virtual screening (FBVS) strategy to identify chemically tractable starting points for the inhibition of KLK6 and KLK7.

title: Systematic Analysis of Stromal-Epithelial Crosstalk Reveals the FGF21-FGFR3 Axis as a Key Driver of Corneal Wound Healing
creator: Zhe Zhu, Hongran Zhao, Qingjun Zhou, Shengqian Dou, Weiyun Shi
description: PurposeCorneal epithelial defects are a significant clinical problem and pose a severe threat to vision. However, their underlying mechanisms remain largely elusive. Here, we used single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and constructed cell-cell communication networks between corneal stromal cells (CSCs) and epithelial cells (CEpCs) to elucidate the pathological mechanism underlying corneal epithelial wound repair.

title: The Distinct Structural Propensities of Poly-C, A, and U Single-Stranded RNA
creator: Tong Wang, Weiwei He, Scout Fronhofer, Serdal Kirmizialtin, Lois Pollack
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Homopolymeric single-stranded RNAs (ssRNAs) are common biological motifs, yet their sequence-dependent solution structures remain incompletely defined. Particularly, rC30 and rA30 have not been characterized with atomic detail. Using optimized force fields, we integrate small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) with SAXS-driven molecular dynamics to generate and refine conformational ensembles for thirty-nucleotide-long strands of poly­(rA), poly­(rC), and poly­(rU) (rA30, rC30, and rU30) in identical buffers. Scattering profiles are computed from refined MD-generated ensembles and accurately reproduce the SAXS measurements.

title: Intra‐Islet Paracrine Regulation of Glucagon Secretion During Hypoglycemia, Euglycemia, and Hyperglycemia
creator: Samaneh Fatehi, Jonathan V Rocheleau, Michael C Riddell
description: The regulation of glucagon and insulin secretion, from pancreatic α‐ and β‐cells, respectively, is essential for maintaining blood glucose within the physiological set point. Insulin secretion is stimulated as glucose rises from euglycemia, with incretin hormones modulating the secretion in a glucose‐dependent manner. Glucagon secretion is elevated with hypoglycemia but also with hyperglycemia.

title: A Graph‐Based Machine Learning Framework to Assign Empirical Interaction Parameters for Novel Molecules
creator: Yao Fu, Martin Stroet, Megan L O'Mara
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of novel molecules are essential to modern drug discovery and related fields that require large‐scale sampling of chemical space. However, obtaining accurate and robust force field parameters for novel molecules remains a major challenge. One approach to this problem is to perform quantum chemical calculations on a per‐molecule basis, but doing so on a large scale is prohibitively expensive.

title: Prokaryotic Novelty and Metabolic Diversity in the Tagoro Shallow Hydrothermal System (Canary Islands, Spain)
creator: Clàudia Pérez‐Barrancos, Eugenio Fraile‐Nuez, José Antonio Lozano‐Rodríguez, María Isabel Díaz‐Durán, Carmen Presas‐Navarro, Jesús M. Arrieta
description: The shallow hydrothermal system of the Tagoro submarine volcano (Canary Islands, Spain) has been discharging low‐temperature, nutrient‐rich, acidic fluids high in CO2 and H2S since March 2012. Despite influencing local microbial communities, the effects of these hydrothermal fluids on community structure and diversity across spatial gradients remain poorly understood.

title: Myositis-specific and myositis-associated autoantibodies in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies: An EASI survey on current clinical and laboratory practices
creator: W.H.M. Vroemen, M.A. Dragon-Durey, Y. Allenbach, T. Berki, S. Čučnik, M. Infantino, E. Neves, E. Nagy, N. Pascu, D. Patel, M. Probst, L. Taylor, J.G.M.C. Damoiseaux, C. Bonroy
description: ObjectivesDetection of myositis-specific and myositis associated autoantibodies (MSA/MAA) aids in classification, diagnosis, and risk stratification of idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM). To identify opportunities for harmonization, we assessed laboratory and clinical variability in IIM serological testing.MethodsThe European Autoimmunity Standardisation Initiative (EASI) developed questionnaires targeting laboratory medicine specialists and clinicians addressing test initiation, testing methods and algorithms, reporting and interpretation.

title: Skin organoid-derived exosomes in a hydrogel system potentiate skin wound healing
creator: Tao Yang, Wen Zheng, Yue Li, Yingshi Li, Zhuxian Wang, Qiuyu Chen, Yangmeihui Wang, Xiaoye Shi, Jun Liu, Bin Yang
description: Skin wounds, whether acute or chronic, remain a major clinical challenge due to their complex healing processes involving inflammation, angiogenesis, and tissue remodeling. While stem cell-derived exosomes offer a promising cell-free therapeutic approach, their clinical translation is limited by rapid clearance and insufficient tissue-specificity.

title: Effectiveness of dietary, physical activity, and lifestyle interventions on weight and cardiometabolic outcomes in adults with overweight or obesity: an umbrella review of 112 systematic reviews and meta-analyses from 50 countries
creator: Mahesh Kumar Mummadi, Subbarao M. Gavaravarapu, Samarasimha N. Reddy, Karthikeyan Ramanujam, Ritika Prakash, Sudhakar Reddy Vadde, Raghavendra Pandurangi, Priyanka G. Bansal, Ranadip Chowdhury, Bharati Kulkarni
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundOverweight and obesity affect an estimated 2.5 billion adults worldwide. Reviews of single treatment modalities are abundant, but clinicians lack one appraised comparison of nutrition therapy, physical activity, and behavioural modification across outcomes and treatment durations.MethodsThis was an umbrella review and meta-analysis of systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials in adults aged 18 years or older with overweight or obesity. PubMed was searched (2015–2025) with backward and forward citation tracking.

title: From heat-treatment maps to repairable tooling of LPBF-produced M789 maraging stainless steel
creator: Ludmila Kučerová, Michal Ackermann, Andrea Málková, Jiří Šafka, Pavel Žlábek, Michal Kaufman
description: SummaryLaser powder bed fusion (LPBF) can produce corrosion-resistant, ultra-high-strength maraging stainless steels for tooling, but post-processing routes balancing strength, toughness, thermal stability, and repairability remain unclear. We establish an internally consistent heat-treatment map for cobalt-free M789 across direct aging, solution annealing, and combined routes. As-built material exhibited 1.

title: Intravenous ferric carboxymaltose and exercise capacity in iron-deficient kidney transplant recipients: a randomised, placebo-controlled trial in the Netherlands
creator: Joanna Sophia J Vinke, Michele F Eisenga, Amarens van der Vaart, Caspar J van Lieshout, Helma WGM Dolmans, Peter van der Meer, Jozine M ter Maaten, Jacoba M Spikman, Aaltje L Ziengs, Jenny E Kootstra-Ros, Ilja M Nolte, Carlo GM Gaillard, Margriet FC de Jong, Stefan P Berger, Jan-Stephan F Sanders, S
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryBackgroundWhether correction of iron deficiency improves functional outcomes after kidney transplantation is unknown. We evaluated intravenous ferric carboxymaltose for improving exercise capacity in iron-deficient kidney transplant recipients.MethodsIn this multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial, adult kidney transplant recipients with iron deficiency (ferritin <100 μg/L or 100–299 μg/L with transferrin saturation <20%) at least six months post-transplantation were recruited at two Dutch university hospitals between 7 October 2019 and 16 February 2024.

title: Multiscale assessment of transboundary water-food-energy nexus under climate change in Irtysh River Basin
creator: Xialin Wang, Xiaoning Wang, Hanyu Jin, Hongrui Liu, Yanbo Li
description: SummaryClimate change is intensifying water scarcity and amplifying upstream-downstream tensions in transboundary river basins, particularly in Central Asia. We present a multiscale framework integrating hydrological dynamics with the water-food-energy (WFE) nexus to assess climate-driven cross-sectoral trade-offs in Irtysh River Basin.

title: Pediatric yeast fungaemia species patterns, resistance profiles, and outcomes: a 20-year surveillance study in Paris, France
creator: Fanny Alby-Laurent, Thomas Obadia, Maud Gits-Muselli, Marie-Elisabeth Bougnoux, Benoit Brethon, Patricia Mariani, Juliette Guitard, Françoise Botterel, Elisabeth Chachaty, Karine Boukris-Sitbon, Alexandre Alanio, Alexandre Alanio, Adela Angoulvant, Nawel Ait-Ammar, Christine Bonnal, Sophie Brun, Nai
description: SummaryBackgroundThe epidemiology of pediatric yeast bloodstream infections remains poorly characterized in high-income settings despite global shifts over the past two decades. As fungal species distribution varies geographically, national surveillance is essential. In France, recent reports have focused predominantly on adults, leaving a significant evidence gap for children.

title: A Review of Senescence‐Associated Secretory Phenotype‐Mediated Remodeling of the Tumor Microenvironment: Implications for Cancer Progression and Therapy
creator: Sneha Pallatt, Sibin Nambidi, Antara Banerjee, Surajit Pathak
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCellular senescence influences cancer progression through irreversible cell‐cycle arrest, immune surveillance, and paracrine signaling mediated by the senescence‐associated secretory phenotype (SASP). SASP comprises inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, growth factors, and matrix‐remodeling enzymes that regulate the tumor microenvironment (TME).ObjectiveThis review describes the current evidence on the mechanisms of SASP induction, its condition‐dependent roles in cancer, TME remodeling, and emerging strategies targeting senescent cells and SASP signaling.MethodsRelevant literature was identified through searches on PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar using keywords related to

title: Extraordinary movements connecting distant ecosystems by African wild dogs ( L ycaon pictus)
creator: Scott Creel, Stephani Matsushima, Henry Mwape, Bridget Mayani‐Nkhoma, Kachama Banda, Ben Goodheart, Johnathan Reyes de Merkle, Anna Kusler, Daan Smit, Johane Njobvu, Moses Muwowo, Reuben Kabungo, Michelo Mungolo, Mwamba Sichande, Catherine Sun, Carolyn A. Sanguinetti, Charlotte Krag, Lucky Chama, Mw
description: e Ellender, David Christianson, Egil Dröge, Matthew S. Becker Published: 2026 EWD‐1355, a 3‐year‐old African wild dog (Lycaon pictus), dispersed from the Luamfwa pack in Zambia's South Luangwa National Park in October of 2021, together with two of her littermate sisters.

title: Social Media Addiction in Adolescents and the Effect of Emotional Intelligence on Ghosting
creator: Ramazan İnci, Sevgi Köroğlu Gökbel, Hatice Kiliçkiran Doğan, Nursel Gül, Kübra Yesin, Metin Yıldız
description: Objective This study was conducted to examine the effect of social media addiction and emotional intelligence on ghosting among adolescents. Methods This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted between June and September 2025 using an online survey method. The study was conducted with 425 adolescents aged 10–19 years living in Batman, Türkiye. R programming language 4.1.3, G*Power 3.

title: Topical Epidermal Growth Factor in Acne Vulgaris and Acne‐Related Sequelae: Mechanistic Rationale, Clinical Evidence, and Formulation Challenges
creator: Nasim Gholizadeh, Ghasem Rahmatpour Rokni, Maryam Sahafi, Omid Mohaghegh, Ardalan Etemadzadeh, Reyhaneh Pasandipour, Hamed Fakhrabadi, Ghazal Zoghi
description: BackgroundAcne vulgaris (AV) is a common chronic inflammatory skin disorder, particularly among adolescents and young adults, and its management remains limited by variable treatment response, poor adherence, and treatment‐related adverse effects.AimsThis review critically evaluates the mechanistic rationale, clinical evidence, safety considerations, and formulation challenges relating to topical epidermal growth factor (EGF) in active acne vulgaris and acne‐related sequelae.

title: Adjunctive Use of Platelet‐Rich Plasma With Fractional CO2 Laser Versus Standalone Laser Therapy for the Treatment of Atrophic Acne Scarring: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
creator: Qiang Hu, Shuang Sui, Zhenghua Yang, Kaiwen Zhang, Haibo Wang
description: BackgroundAtrophic acne scars are a common and persistent sequela of inflammatory acne. Fractional CO2 laser treatment promotes collagen production and scar remodeling but is often associated with adverse effects such as prolonged erythema, edema, and hyperpigmentation. Adjunctive use of platelet‐rich plasma (PRP) has been proposed to enhance efficacy and reduce complications, yet existing evidence remains inconsistent.

title: 679. From Bench to Clinic: Zatolmilast and the Translation of Neurobiology Research into a Targeted Therapy for Fragile X Syndrome
creator: J C Gomez
description: BackgroundDrug development in Fragile X syndrome (FXS) has been challenging with multiple development programs failing to achieve positive pivotal study results over decades of continued effort. Meanwhile translational research has continued to lead to the identification of clinically relevant biological pathways within FXS and subsequently the discovery of new investigational therapies.

title: 462. Mass spectrometry imaging uncovers species-specific dopaminergic effects of tetrabenazine in rodents
creator: S Diez, E Koros, Z Balla, S Almeida-Correa, J F Du Hoffmann, M Becker, K M Danzer, C T Wotjak
description: BackgroundTetrabenazine (TBZ) is a known inhibitor of the vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2), resulting in reduced monoaminergic signaling, including dopamine. Previous internal behavioral studies have demonstrated that TBZ exerts a noticeably stronger impact on motivational behavior in rats compared to mice. However, the underlying neurochemical mechanisms responsible for these species-specific differences remain unclear.

title: 852. Preclinical models of non dopaminergic antipsychotics
creator: G Rutigliano
description: BackgroundCurrent antipsychotic treatments primarily rely on dopamine D2 receptor antagonism and show limited efficacy for negative and cognitive symptoms, as well as in treatment-resistant schizophrenia. Trace amine-associated receptor 1 (TAAR1) agonists represent a promising non-dopaminergic approach with a distinct mechanism of action.

title: 325. Real-world data on the abuse potential of medications for the treatment of insomnia
creator: P Saskin, W V McCall, D Neubauer, A Crucitti, P-P Luyet, R Jaziri, C Vaillant, N Burton
description: BackgroundInsomnia disorder is a chronic medical condition that is estimated to affect 12% of adults. Although CBTi is recognized as an important first line therapy it can be challenging to access and implement, resulting in problems with compliance. As a result many individuals with insomnia disorder receive medication treatment, often for prolonged periods of time.

title: 728. Environmental, psychiatric, and genetic predictors of alcohol use disorder criterion count
creator: P J Na, J D Deak, D F Levey, H R Kranzler, R H Pietrzak, J Gelernter
description: BackgroundGenetic and environmental factors, and psychiatric traits, contribute to risk for alcohol use disorder (AUD) and other substance use disorders (SUDs) and traits. Weighing the importance of the different kinds of contribution to risk is important in understanding risk prediction – which may be important clinically -- and in formulating prevention and treatment strategies.

title: 265. Physical activity, weekend catch-up sleep, and depressive symptoms: mediating effects of high-sensitivity C-reactive protein
creator: S-Y Kim, D Ho, W-J Lim
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundEmerging evidence suggests that inflammation may play a key role in depression, and lifestyle factors such as physical activity and weekend catch-up sleep may reduce inflammation—reflected by lower CRP levels—which could help alleviate depressive symptoms.Aims & ObjectivesWe aimed to examine the effect of physical activity (PA) and weekend catch-up sleep (WCS) on depressive symptoms by evaluating their effects on high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) levels.MethodData were collected from 10,715 adults aged ≥ 19 years. PA and depressive symptoms were assessed using self-report scales.

title: 181. Integrating clinical profiles and microRNAs to uncover molecular mechanisms in treatment-resistant schizophrenia
creator: L Vellucci, P Mirra, A Nasti, D Formisano, A Barone, F Iannotta, M Ciccarelli, D Conza, C Miele, F Iasevoli, F Beguinot, A de Bartolomeis
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundTreatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS), defined as the persistence of symptoms despite adequate antipsychotic treatment, remains frequently underrecognized, with clozapine, the gold standard, introduced only after an average delay of 4–9 years. In this study, we aimed to identify which Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) factors, executive function measures, and selected microRNAs (miRNAs) are most strongly associated with TRS, and to investigate the molecular underpinnings targeted by these miRNAs, thereby hypothesizing aberrant mechanisms contributing to the TRS condition.Aims & ObjectivesThis study sought to

title: 570. A study on the similarities and differences in brain functional connectivity alterations in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder
creator: Y Sun, Y Xing, Q Bo, L Zhao, Y Han, Z Chen, C Wang
description: BackgroundSchizophrenia (SZ) and bipolar disorder (BD) are common severe mental disorders. Although clear diagnostic boundaries exist between the two disorders, they share overlaps in certain clinical symptoms and abnormal brain network functions. Recent neuroimaging studies have shown both specific differences and common alterations in resting-state brain network functional connectivity (FC) between SZ and BD.

title: 753. The Mechanism of Ketamine’s Anti-Suicidal Action: From Glutamatergic Surge to Neuroplasticity via the Opioid-Attachment Interface
creator: A Solomon, Y Domany
description: BackgroundA critical gap exists in understanding the biological mechanism linking ketamine’s rapid anti-suicidal effects to the Interpersonal Theory of Suicide (IPTS). While the "Kinetic Mismatch" between acute relief and delayed synaptogenesis is well-known, current models overlook how ketamine modulates “Thwarted Belongingness” (a core IPTS pillar) and the attachment anxiety that drives suicidal risk in the acute phase.

title: 378. Achieving remission in OCD: challenges and opportunities
creator: S Pallanti
description: BackgroundDespite the availability of evidence-based pharmacological and psychotherapeutic treatments for obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD), achieving full remission remains a major clinical challenge. A substantial proportion of patients show only partial response, with persistent symptoms, functional impairment, and reduced quality of life. This has shifted the therapeutic focus from symptomatic improvement to remission as the primary and clinically meaningful outcome.

title: 576. Alprazolam for symptom relief: addressing the more troublesome features of anxiety disorders
creator: S Shirol, S Awasthi, A Fagiolini, K Subramaniam, P Purushottamahanti
description: BackgroundAnxiety disorders are the world’s most common mental disorders, affecting 359 million people in 20211, and a lifetime prevalence up to 33.7%2. Among those with anxiety disorders, patients having generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) demonstrate a considerable degree of impairment and disability resulting in significant economic burden, especially with an increase in health care resource utilisation(22%)3.

title: 860. Glutamatergic Signaling and Neuroplasticity in Mood Disorders: A Historical Perspective from Preclinical Discoveries to Clinical Translation
creator: G Gobbi
description: BackgroundWhile the monoaminergic hypothesis has long dominated the treatment of mood disorders, its limitations have prompted the exploration of alternative mechanisms. Early work by Skolnick et al. (1996) demonstrated that chronic antidepressant treatment induces adaptive changes in N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors, suggesting glutamatergic signaling as a convergent pathway in antidepressant action.

title: 776. Bridging the divide: can we use human living cell models to link studies in human postmortem brain and live participants?
creator: S Berretta
description: BackgroundInvestigations on the biological underpinnings of psychosis spectrum disorders (PSDs) point to the involvement of both neuronal and glia populations, within neural circuits involved in emotion regulation and executive functions. A key question is how changes in these different cell types relate to one another, i.e.

title: 770. Long-Term Clinical Trajectory Following Short-Term Digital Therapeutics in Adolescents with Autism: Preliminary Findings from a Multicenter Expansion Study
creator: T Y Choi, S Chang, J Lee
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPharmacological treatments for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) primarily target associated behavioral symptoms such as irritability, while core social communication deficits remain insufficiently addressed. Digital therapeutics (DTx) have emerged as scalable, non-pharmacological interventions designed to improve social functioning. NDTx-01 is a mobile-based social skills training (SST) digital therapeutic that previously demonstrated significant short-term improvements in adaptive behavior, as measured by the Korean Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales (K-VABS), and social responsiveness, assessed by the Social Responsiveness Scale-2 (SRS-2), following a 6-week intervention.

title: 529. **Rafaelsen Award Presentation** Cognitive function and the risk of later onset of depression in healthy individuals: a 10-year longitudinal study
creator: A Sankar, B Ozenne, V Dam, E Beaman, L Kessing, P Fisher, G Knudsen, K Miskowiak, V Frokjær
description: BackgroundCognitive impairments are common in individuals with depression, but their role in the etiology of the disorder remains unclear.Aims & ObjectivesIn this 10-year longitudinal study, we tested whether cognitive function is associated with a risk for developing future first-episode depression in individuals without prior psychiatric diagnoses.

title: 180. Effects of MC-100093, GLT-1 enhancer, in mesocorticolimbic brain regions of C57BL/6 mouse exposed to hydrocodone overdose using comprehensive laboratory monitoring system
creator: Y Sari, W Wong, W Childers, M Abou-Gharbia
description: BackgroundChronic exposure and overdose of opioid cause neurotoxicity through alterations of several neurotransmitters, including glutamate. Targeting glutamate transporter 1 (GLT-1) may attenuate the effects of chronic exposure to drugs of abuse. Thus, the effects of novel GLT-1 enhancer, MC-100093, and β-lactam ceftriaxone, were evaluated in C57BL/6 mice exposed to hydrocodone overdose.

title: 652. A three-year community-based longitudinal study of transcranial direct current stimulation
creator: K P Kwak
description: BackgroundAs population aging accelerates, cognitive decline in community-dwelling older adults with normal cognition and mild cognitive impairment has become a significant public health issue. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is a safe, non-invasive intervention with potential cognitive benefits, but evidence on its long-term effects is limited.

title: The Agency of Forced Migrants: Historical Perspectives
creator: Philipp Strobl, Christoph Rass, Kerstin von Lingen, Philipp Strobl, Christoph Rass, Kerstin von Lingen
description: This introduction sets out the thematic and methodological framework of a special issue on historical refugee agency in the aftermath of the Second World War. It situates the volume within historiographical debates that move beyond narratives of passive victimization, instead foregrounding how refugees actively shaped their lives and the regimes that sought to govern them.

title: 749. Safety, tolerability, and efficacy data of 60 Hz white light stimulation in major depressive disorder
creator: M T Ferretti, R Pelesof, F Leesch, A Venturino, A Brunoni, K Vidal
description: BackgroundPrevious preclinical and healthy volunteer studies have demonstrated that flickering white light at 60 Hz induces neuroplasticity while being safe and well-tolerated. These results suggest a potential application of flickering light at 60 Hz for the treatment of neuropsychiatric conditions, including depression.

title: 816. Frontal structural network vulnerability and peripheral immune dysregulation in major depressive disorder: diagnostic and prognostic implications
creator: W Du, M Yuan, Z Gao, H Li, S Lui, W Zhang
description: BackgroundImmune dysregulation has been increasingly implicated in major depressive disorder (MDD), yet it remains unclear how peripheral immune alterations interact with brain structure and whether these mechanisms differentially contribute to diagnosis and prognosis. In particular, the relative clinical value of immune markers versus cortical structural vulnerability has not been systematically evaluated.

title: 173. Cytochrome variability and the escalation of clinical complexity in neurodevelopmental disorders
creator: M Geiser, J Convertini, V Guinchat
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundChallenging behaviors (CB), including aggression, self-injury, and severe agitation, are a major cause of suffering and institutionalization in individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD). Their multifactorial nature often leads to empirical psychopharmacological escalation and polypharmacy.

title: Comparación de impuestos como porcentaje del precio de las bebidas azucaradas en América Latina y el Caribe*
creator: Maxime Roche, Miriam Alvarado, Rosa Carolina Sandoval, Fabio da Silva Gomes, Guillermo Paraje
description: RESUMENObjetivo.Los impuestos selectivos al consumo pueden utilizarse para reducir el consumo de bebidas azucaradas, un importante factor de riesgo prevenible de las enfermedades no transmisibles. El objetivo de este estudio es comparar nuevos indicadores estandarizados del nivel de impuestos aplicados a las bebidas azucaradas como porcentaje del precio en las distintas categorías de bebidas en América Latina y el Caribe.Método.

title: Fibrin sealant-enhanced single-port LLS with cervical preservation and “homemade” mesh: an innovative surgical technique for pelvic organ prolapse
creator: Yuan-Qin Gou, Ning Xu, Yuan-Hong Li
description: Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) is a common condition that significantly impacts patients’ quality of life, with a notably high incidence among postmenopausal women. While laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy remains the gold standard for surgical management, laparoscopic lateral suspension (LLS) has gained increasing attention as an effective alternative, offering comparable outcomes and distinct advantages.

title: Hypercalcemia in a Patient With Spinal Tuberculosis and Aspergillus Co‐Infection: A Case‐Report
creator: Negin Parsa, Amirpasha Amlelshahbaz, Hamidreza Soltani
description: BackgroundTuberculosis (TB), one of the leading infectious causes of mortality worldwide, may disseminate hematogenously and result in extrapulmonary manifestations. Spinal tuberculosis (ST) is an uncommon but serious form of extrapulmonary TB. In addition, TB may predispose patient to opportunistic infections, including Aspergillus species.Case PresentationA 62‐year‐old man presented with chronic back pain and sudden paraplegia.

title: Contraceptive implant removal: Case report and the role of an ultrasound-trained anesthesiologist in perioperative localization and regional anesthesia
creator: Austin T. Nguyen, Matthew W. Swisher
description: BackgroundContraceptive implants offer a long-term reversible option for contraception. While palpable implants can be removed under local anesthesia in an office setting, nonpalpable implants can present greater safety challenges and may increase the overall complication rate of removal.Case presentationWe present the case of a 28 year-old female who presented for an elective upper extremity contraceptive implant removal.

title: 115. The moderating effect of vitamin D between depressive symptoms and light exposure: a 1-year comparative cohort study
creator: C-I Liu, C-E Chang, I-M Chen, H-C Chen, C-M Liu, C-H Chen, W-Y Chen, P-H Kuo
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMajor depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar disorder (BD) often exhibit mood fluctuations linked to seasonal changes. Vitamin D level and light exposure have been proposed to influence the mood symptoms, while the interaction between them has not been studied.Aims & ObjectivesThis study investigates seasonal variations in light exposure and vitamin D levels in individuals with mood disorders, and explores the interaction between mood symptoms, vitamin D level and light exposure.MethodThis longitudinal study included individuals aged 20–70 diagnosed with MDD or BD according

title: 846. Inconsistent trial risk-of-bias judgements across psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy systematic reviews
creator: K Henke-Ciążyńska, D Pankowski, B Helfer
description: BackgroundSystematic reviews with meta-analyses (SR-MAs) of psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy (PAP) guide clinical and policy decisions. Their trustworthiness depends, in part, on how consistently different SR-MAs assess risk of bias (RoB) in the same underlying randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and how transparently those judgments are justified.

title: Post-infarction left ventricular pseudoaneurysm with septal rupture: a case report
creator: Bibissara Yerekesh, Zhannat Nurumova, Anel Assylbekova, Rustem Tuleutayev, Dmitriy Gebel, Leila Sani, Saltanat Altybayeva, Alima Turemuratova
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Despite advances in reperfusion therapy, acute myocardial infarction may still lead to rare, life-threatening mechanical complications. We describe the case of a 58-year-old man who developed progressive heart failure two months after an untreated anterior myocardial infarction. Multimodality imaging demonstrated a large left ventricular apical pseudoaneurysm with post-infarction ventricular septal rupture into the right ventricle, resulting in a significant left-to-right shunt. The patient underwent successful aneurysmectomy, closure of the septal defect, and coronary artery bypass grafting.

title: 820. α6GABAA receptors as novel targets for ADHD therapy: A proof-of-concept study in MK-801-treated juvenile mice
creator: Y-H Lee, C-C Lu, H-J Lee, A Mouri, D Sharmin, J Cook, T Nabeshima, W Sieghart, L-C Chiou
description: BackgroundAttention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is associated with cerebellar abnormalities and altered cortico–striatal–cerebellar circuitry. Animal models indicate cerebellar microcircuit dysfunction, including reduced inhibitory control of granule cells (GCs). GABAA receptors containing the Gabra6-encoded α6 subunit (α6GABAARs) are highly enriched in the cerebellar GCs and regulate their excitability.

title: 649. A clinical review of bupropion and pain
creator: P Chue, H Shaltout, E Owusu, J Chue, M Tate
description: BackgroundAntidepressants have been demonstrated to have analgesic and anti-inflammatory activity in animal models and clinical settings. Analgesic effects appear to be independent of mood. While tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) have been used historically off-label for neuropathic and fibromyalgia pain, the selective serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) duloxetine and milnacipran, and pregabalin have formal indications for the latter.

title: 722. Predictors of therapeutic response to LSD in anxiety: short- and long-term outcomes
creator: F Holze, F Müller, P Gasser, M Liechti
description: BackgroundAnxiety disorders are a major health burden and current treatment options yield unsatisfactory results. Psychedelics, such as lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) that act via agonism on serotonin 2A receptors, have recently been shown to be effective in the treatment of anxiety symptoms.

title: Laparoscopic round‑ligament duodenostomy synchronized with posterior mediastinal reconstruction
creator: Takeshi Matsubara, Yoko Senaha, Hiroki Okamura, Shunsuke Kaji, Hikota Hayashi, Kazunari Ishitobi, Takahito Taniura, Takayuki Tanaka, Tetsu Yamamoto, Masaaki Hidaka
description: INTRODUCTION: Esophagectomy is a highly invasive procedure, and early enteral nutrition supports recovery. Feeding jejunostomy is common but may cause fixation-related mechanical complications. To address these issues, a duodenostomy using the hepatic round ligament was adapted to a fully laparoscopic approach.

title: 541. Serum neurofilament light chain is associated with psychotic remission, independent of antipsychotic treatment in schizophrenia
creator: P-Y Chen, M-C Huang
description: BackgroundSchizophrenia involves neuroaxonal disruption linked to psychotic symptoms and clinical remission. Blood neurofilament light chain (NfL), a neuronal scaffolding protein essential for axonal integrity and synaptic activity, is released into the cerebrospinal fluid and blood upon neurodegeneration. Often described as a "troponin for the brain," NfL was recently FDA-approved as a surrogate endpoint for neuroaxonal injury.

title: The CXCL12/CXCR4 Axis in Sepsis-Induced Acute Lung Injury: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential
creator: Renwei Luo, Qinglu Fan, Qingyun Chen, Zhihao Nie, Lingxuan Dan, Songping Xie, Arumugam R Jayakumar
description: Sepsis remains a major cause of acute lung injury (ALI) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), conditions characterized by high mortality and limited therapeutic options. Among the diverse inflammatory pathways implicated in their pathogenesis, the CXCL12/CXCR4 chemokine axis has gained increasing attention for its dual capacity to drive acute inflammation while also supporting tissue repair.

title: 653. Effects of 10Hz transcranial focused ultrasound stimulation at the posterior cingulate cortex on cerebral glucose metabolism – a pilot fPET study
creator: G M Godbersen, M Lückel, C Milz, P Falb, A Harouak, S Vijayakumar, P Stöhrmann, K Al Barede, G Dörl, M Reed, S Rasul, M Hacker, D Rujescu, T O Bergmann, A Hahn, R Lanzenberger
description: BackgroundTranscranial focused ultrasound stimulation (TUS) is emerging as a promising method for non-invasive and safe modulation of neuronal activity throughout the human brain [1]. Although several centers worldwide have started to investigate TUS in patient collectives, dosing of sonication parameters remains challenging. This is because conventional imaging approaches are limited in objectively measuring stimulation effects.

title: Extracranial Spread of Meningiomas: Molecular Determinants, Diagnostic Pathways, and Lessons From Three Thoracic Metastases
creator: Victor A Perez-Gutierrez, Muneeb Ahmed, Gopal Krishna B, Kari Hird, Michael Balatico, Muhammad Atif Waqar, Jefferson Chambers, Sikandar Ansari
description: Meningiomas are the most common primary intracranial neoplasms of all brain tumors. Although the majority are benign, a subset displays aggressive behavior characterized by recurrence, anaplastic transformation, or, rarely, extracranial metastasis. Lung parenchyma represents the most frequent site of spread, followed by mediastinal and pleural involvement. Despite recent advances in molecular characterization, predicting metastatic potential remains challenging.

title: Biomechanical Evolution in Longitudinal Analysis of Lumbar Stress Injuries in Fast Bowlers: A Systematic Review
creator: C Arun, Sai Aditya Raman, Nimishaanth SS, Thiagarajan KA, Arumugam Sivaraman
description: Fast bowling involves a highly complex and physically demanding motion sequence, placing fast bowlers under substantially greater workloads than other cricketing roles. Consequently, they experience a disproportionately high incidence of injuries, particularly to the lower back, with lumbar stress fractures being especially common in adolescent bowlers.

title: 718. How evidence shapes implementation: beware the extrapolation fallacy
creator: E Schenberg
description: BackgroundAs psychedelic therapies advance toward regulatory approval worldwide, significant questions arise about the adequacy of traditional evidence hierarchies for evaluating these complex interventions. Psychedelic-assisted therapies combine pharmacological, psychological, contextual, and phenomenological elements that challenge conventional randomized controlled trial (RCT) designs.

title: Paclitaxel-Induced Hypertriglyceridemia Complicated by Acute Pancreatitis: A Case Report
creator: Rahul Chowdhary, Kirti Arora, Rishi Chowdhary, Sarmand Jameel, Manjeet K Goyal, Elliot Sorrell
description: Paclitaxel, a widely used chemotherapy agent, has been associated with various adverse effects, including hypertriglyceridemia and, rarely, acute pancreatitis. The potential for paclitaxel to trigger lipid metabolism disturbances necessitates close monitoring of lipid profiles in patients undergoing treatment.We report the case of a 48-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer who developed acute pancreatitis following paclitaxel chemotherapy.

title: Giant Cell Arteritis Following Dental Procedure
creator: Ahmad Jabaiah
description: Giant cell arteritis (GCA), also known as temporal arteritis, is a chronic vasculitis affecting large- and medium-sized arteries in patients over 50 years old. Untreated GCA can cause serious morbidity like irreversible vision loss, aneurysms, or stroke. We present a case of a patient who developed an acute headache and trismus within hours of undergoing a root canal treatment.

title: Research Progress on the Regulatory Mechanisms of Gut Microbiota in Methamphetamine Addiction and Targeted Interventions
creator: Jihao Yang, Yishuang Dai, Jia Li
description: Methamphetamine (METH) is a globally prevalent, highly addictive synthetic psychostimulant, for which no FDA‐approved pharmacotherapy is currently available for METH use disorder (MUD). The microbiota–gut–brain axis has been well established as a key regulatory pathway in substance use disorders, yet its specific mechanistic basis and translational potential in METH addiction remain to be systematically elucidated.

title: 640. Antidepressants engage estrogen receptor alpha and its intracellular signaling components
creator: S Arjmand, M Rezaei, D Sardella, C Cecchi Kaadt, R Rossi, C Vægter, H Müller, J Sahana, M Nielsen, U Simonsen, S Sinning, A Landau, G Wegener, S Joca, C Biojone
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMajor depressive disorder (MDD) exhibits pronounced sex differences in prevalence, symptom severity, and treatment response, implicating a possible role for sex steroid signaling in mood regulation. Mood disturbances linked to reproductive life stages, such as premenstrual syndrome (PMS), premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), postpartum depression, perimenopausal, and postmenopausal depression, highlight the sensitivity of affective states to fluctuations in ovarian hormones, particularly estrogen. Estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) mediates both classical genomic effects and rapid extranuclear signaling through kinase pathways.

title: Do the Changes in Hip Lateralization Up to One-Year Post-reduction in Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip Affect Those Observed at the Age of Four?
creator: Yohei Tomaru, Takashi Saisu, Makoto Kamegaya, Yasuhiro Oikawa, Akitoshi Sakuma, Jun Kakizaki, Yuko Segawa, Yuta Tsukagoshi, Daisuke Nozawa, Hiroshi Kamada
description: BackgroundTreatment outcomes of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) are evaluated by various factors. Although it is reported that centripetality is important for the development of the acetabulum in DDH, only a limited number of studies have examined the changes in lateralization following reduction.

title: Prognostic Value of Spatial Trajectory of J‐Point Amplitude Across Left Precordial Leads in a Community‐Based Population
creator: Chenhui Tai, Zhe Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionEarly repolarization has historically been regarded as benign in many settings, although specific J‐point features have been linked to adverse outcomes. Whether spatial variation in J‐point amplitude across adjacent precordial leads carries prognostic information remains unclear.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included participants aged 40–90 years without self‐reported myocardial infarction or heart failure from the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES‐III). Latent class trajectory analysis was used to identify spatial trajectories of J‐point amplitude across leads V4–V6.

title: The Gifted Outlier in Academic Medicine: Toward a Balanced Framework for Recognizing Diverse Excellence
creator: Dimitrios Moris
description: Academic medicine increasingly evaluates faculty through quantifiable productivity metrics, including publication counts, citation indices, and grant funding. Within this environment, a small subset of clinicians and physician-scientists produce scholarly output at rates far exceeding disciplinary norms. These highly productive individuals can accelerate innovation, attract trainees, and elevate institutional reputation.

title: Aquifer Microbial Communities Differentially Display Metabolisms Capable of Secondary Effects on Uranium Speciation Across a Former Metal Processing Site
creator: Catherine J Pettinger, Allondra M Woods, Raymond H Johnson, Charles J Paradis, Erica L‐W Majumder
description: Groundwater contamination presents worldwide challenges, yet remediation solutions in variably oxidized regions are limited, with co‐interactions between contaminant metals and microbial reactions occurring. Here we present a genomic and metabolic study into the biogeochemistry of a uranium‐contaminated surficial aquifer site in Riverton, WY. We identified unique communities that varied based on geochemistry, geography, and compartment, matching other microbial subsurface studies.

title: 618. Modulation of hippocampal fear engrams reveals circuit mechanisms linking maladaptive fear, memory deficits, and depressive-like behaviour
creator: L P Iglesias, M C van den Oever, G Wegener, S Joca
description: BackgroundClassic PTSD symptoms have been linked to maladaptive fear memory processing, involving fear generalization and impaired extinction learning. In contrast, cognitive and mood symptoms remain understudied, and their link to fear-related mechanisms is unclear.Aims & ObjectivesHere, we investigate the mechanistic link between maladaptive fear, memory impairments and depressive-like behaviour.

title: From Theory to Practice: Serious Game Education in Singapore and Canada
creator: Bill Kapralos, Bina Rai
description: Immersive virtual learning environments (iVLEs) are increasingly used in education, yet their effectiveness is often hindered by educators’ limited knowledge of the design and application of these environments. This chapter thoroughly details two interdisciplinary undergraduate courses whose aim was to introduce students to iVLEs and serious games (SGs) tailored to medical education.

title: 384. S-ketamine, but not R-ketamine, increases the spontaneous firing rate and the AMPA-evoked response of pyramidal neurons in the rat prefrontal cortex
creator: M El Mansari, N Okamoto, P Blier
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundLow-dose racemic ketamine enhances the firing rate and burst activity of rat norepinephrine neurons in the locus coeruleus, as well as the population activity of dopamine neurons in the ventral tegmental area [El Iskandrani et al, 2015].

title: 58. Dissecting Distinct Aspects of Compulsivity Using SIP and 5-CSRTT
creator: P Moazen, C MacMillan, T W Robbins, G Higgins
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundObsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD) is characterized by maladaptive repetitive behaviors and impaired inhibitory control, processes strongly regulated by monoaminergic neurotransmission.Aims & ObjectivesIn this study, we evaluated three clinically relevant compounds with distinct pharmacological profiles: citalopram (selective 5-HT reuptake inhibitor; SSRI), atomoxetine (selective NA reuptake inhibitor; SNRI), and Bupropion (mixed DA/NA reuptake inhibitor; SNRI/SDRI), using two complementary rodent paradigms, Schedule-Induced Polydipsia (SIP) and 5-Choice Serial Reaction Time Task (5-CSRTT) on compulsive behaviors.MethodThirty Wistar rats were used in the SIP paradigm and sixty Long–Evans rats

title: Right Atrial Perforation With Pericardial Effusion and Visceral Pericardial Flap Observed During Pacemaker Implantation: An Echocardiographic Case Report
creator: Frank Jorge Valdez Baez, Cemirame Payan Jimenez, Catherine Merejo Peña, Juanico Cedano Ramirez, Oscar Ortega, Donaldo Collado, Luisa Paulino Lopez, Warenny Montero Morillo, Evelina Severino Marte, Jonathan Rodriguez
description: Pacemaker implantation is a common procedure for the treatment of symptomatic bradyarrhythmias. Although generally safe, it can be associated with serious complications, such as cardiac perforation or pericardial effusion. However, right atrial wall perforation, accompanied by pericardial effusion and visualization of a visceral pericardial flap during the procedure, is an extremely rare and scarcely documented event.

title: 226. Effect of brainspotting in PTSD patients: clinical efficacy and neuropsychopharmacological considerations
creator: M Kawamura, W Ukai, E Hashimoto, E Nishimura, T Ishii, S Iwasaki, M Yamakage
description: BackgroundPost-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is characterized by hyperarousal of emotional memory, avoidance behaviors, and autonomic instability. It is thought to involve an imbalance in the norepinephrine, dopamine, and serotonin neurotransmitter systems mediated by amygdala hyperactivity and functional deficits in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus.

title: 729. From metabolic dysregulation and shared genetic etiology to suicidality: the psychiatric promise and safety debate of GLP-1 receptor agonists
creator: G Fanelli
description: BackgroundMetabolic and psychiatric disorders frequently co-occur, and growing evidence links this overlap to suicide risk. Large population and genomic studies indicate shared alterations in insulin signalling, lipid metabolism, and immune–inflammatory activity, mechanisms also implicated in stress regulation and suicidal behaviour through inflammation, HPA-axis activation, and impaired brain insulin signalling.

title: Paediatric Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis: A 20-Year Single-Centre Retrospective Study of 35 Cases
creator: Faliq Abdullah, Clare Carpenter, Madeleine Adams, Andrew Bamber
description: BackgroundLangerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare proliferative disorder of bone marrow-derived histiocytes that most often affects children. Skeletal involvement is the most frequent manifestation of paediatric LCH, but the lesions can mimic malignancy or infection, posing a diagnostic challenge.

title: 702. Advances in transcranial ultrasonic stimulation (TUS) for non-invasive deep brain neuromodulation in humans
creator: T O Bergmann
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundTranscranial ultrasonic stimulation (TUS) is an emerging technique that comes with the promise of non-invasive deep brain neuromodulation at unprecedented spatial precision, which may revolutionize the treatment of neurological and psychiatric disease.Aims & ObjectivesHowever, two major challenges currently constitute roadblocks for a wider adoption in basic research and clinical application: Firstly, the human skull bone causes significant reflection, aberration, and attenuation of the ultrasound beam, often hampering precise targeting and sufficient target exposure.

title: 257. Patterns of pro re nata prescription of benzodiazepines in the treatment of panic disorder and generalized anxiety disorder
creator: E Moon, J H Seo, M-K Kim, Y Y Chang, H-A Lee, M H Ahn, K S Lee, H-J Seo, W Kim, H-S Suh, K-U Lee
description: BackgroundPanic disorder (PD) and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) present with distinct anxiety profiles, which may lead clinicians to adopt different pharmacological strategies. Benzodiazepines (BDZs) are sometimes prescribed on a pro re nata (PRN) basis to provide rapid relief of acute or situational anxiety, despite guideline recommendations favoring short-term, scheduled use.

title: 726. Invasive neuromodulation for improved outcomes in patients with severe forms of OCD and depression
creator: C Kraus, V Watzal, N Grüll, A Gramser, K Novak
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundRecent results from the largest sham-controlled trial of antidepressant VNS, (N=493) have indicated that quality of life after VNS vs. sham improved, especially in patients with severe and chronic depression (Rush et al., 2025). On the other hand, randomized sham-controlled trials (RCTs) with deep brain stimulation (DBS) in psychiatric populations are scarce with the largest sham-controlled trial in treatment resistant depression demonstrating similar effects in the active as well as in the sham group (Holtzheimer et.

title: Association between Maxillary and Mandibular Length and Crowding in Classes 1, 2, and 3 Skeletal Malocclusion: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
creator: Marshal Lucas, Annapurna Kannan, Vignesh Kailasam
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe relationship between dental crowding and skeletal base length is essential to recognize and consider during the stage of treatment planning.AimTo determine the correlation between maxillary and mandibular length and the quantum of crowding in various malocclusions.MethodsSeven electronic databases—PubMed, OVID, LILACS, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and SciELO—were searched until April 2024 with no restriction on the year of publication.

title: 870. Advancements in the Pharmacologic Treatment of Stuttering
creator: G Maguire
description: BackgroundStuttering is a neuropsychiatric disorder classified in DSM. Stuttering has been reported throughout recorded human history and every language describes stuttering. The disorder typically begins in childhood yet now multiple etiologies have been postulated. Stuttering affects over 4% of children and persists to affect over 1% of all adults.

title: Spectrophotometric Analysis of Intracoronal Bleaching on Crown Discoloration Induced by Various Antibiotic Pastes: An In Vitro Study
creator: Avneet Kaur, Harshit Srivastava, Deepak Raisingani, Ashwini B Prasad, Dileep Soni, Poorva R Sharma
description: AimTo evaluate tooth discoloration after the use of different antibiotic pastes and to examine the effect of intracoronal bleaching on discolored crown.Materials and methodsSingle-rooted maxillary central incisors were collected and sectioned to obtain a standardized root length of 10 mm above the facial cementoenamel junction (CEJ).

title: 206. Adaptive immune system changes related to stress and depression: clinical and preclinical insights
creator: S Kigar, X Shen, S White, X Liu, E Miska, E Bullmore, M-E Lynall
description: BackgroundA challenge for developing new major depressive disorder (MDD) treatments is understanding how non-heritable risk factors like stress alter biological processes. We previously used preclinical animal models to demonstrate chronic psychosocial stress reorganizes the peripheral and meningeal immune milieu and that these shifts are related to depressive-like behavioral change.

title: Comparative Assessment of Microleakage in Nanoformulated and Conventional Glass Ionomer Cement under Simulated Aging: A Stereomicroscopic Study
creator: Aleena Alex, Jessy Paulraj, TM Ngoubinah Pretty, Subhabrata Maiti
description: AimThe aim of the study is to assess the microleakage of nanoformulated and conventional glass ionomer cements (GICs) under simulated aging.Materials and methodsNanoformulated GIC was synthesized by incorporating chitosan-titanium-zirconia-hydroxyapatite (Ch-Ti-Zr-HA) nanoparticles into GIC powder at concentrations of 3%, 5%, and 10%. The materials were characterized using UV-visible diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (UV-DRS) and X-ray diffraction (XRD).

title: 667. Neurotherapies for ADHD: do they work?
creator: K Rubia, A Conti, N Bhozilova, I Eraydim, L Johansson, P Santosh, D Stringer, B Carter, S Cortese
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundStimulant medications are effective for ADHD. However, they have side effects, unknown longer-term effects, poor adherence and are not preferred by children and their parents. Brain modulation has been suggested as a promising non-drug treatment alternative for ADHD as it can target the brain differences established over the last 3 decades of our fMRI studies with minimal and transient side effects.Aims & ObjectivesWe conducted several RCTs of novel neurotherapies for ADHD aimed to modify ADHD relevant brain activation differences with the aim

title: 239. RUNX1 variant rs2236431 is associated with postoperative opioid analgesic requirements in humans
creator: D Nishizawa, J Hasegawa, K Nakayama, K-i Fukuda, T Ichinohe, M Nagashima, M Hayashida, T Trang, K Ikeda
description: BackgroundPostoperative pain management often requires opioid analgesics, but patients show large variability in the doses needed for adequate pain relief. These inter-individual differences hinder effective pain control and may increase the risk of opioid-related adverse outcomes. Genetic factors are estimated to contribute up to 60% of the variability in opioid analgesic response.

title: Carnoy's Solution for the Management of a Pediatric Patient with Adenomatoid Odontogenic Tumor: A Case Report with 2-year Follow-up
creator: Krishna Priya, Y Rajmohan Shetty, Swagata Saha, Naina Kumar, Manju Raman Nair
description: AimAdenomatoid odontogenic tumor (AOT) is a slow-growing, rare lesion that arises from the odontogenic epithelium. It predominantly involves the bone that supports teeth and exhibits different levels of inductive alterations within the connective tissue.Case descriptionA 10-year-old female presented with a missing lower left front tooth since birth.

title: 271. Glymphatic system dysfunction, accelerated brain aging, and inflammation in major psychiatric disorders: a transdiagnostic DTI-ALPS study
creator: Y M Bai, AC-C Yang, M-H Chen, S-J Tsai
description: BackgroundMajor psychiatric disorders, including Schizophrenia (SZ), Bipolar Disorder (BD), and Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), are increasingly recognized as conditions associated with accelerated biological aging and cognitive decline. The glymphatic system, a glial-dependent perivascular network, mediated by aquaporin-4 (AQP4) channels, plays a critical role in clearing metabolic waste and soluble proteins from the central nervous system.

title: 431. Influence of resilience and interpersonal sensitivity on the affective rating of words
creator: T H Ha, S-J Cho, W Myung
description: BackgroundResilience and interpersonal sensitivity are key psychological traits that modulate emotional responses. Resilience modulates emotional responses in a positive and adaptive nature, whereas interpersonal sensitivity does so in a negative and maladaptive manner.Aims & ObjectivesThis study investigated the influence of resilience and interpersonal sensitivity on the evaluation of emotional word valence.

title: Evaluating the Impact of Acupressure and Xylitol Solutions on Reducing Pain Perception in Children Undergoing Local Anesthesia Administration
creator: Lumbini Pathivada, Debalina Baidya, Nishita Garg, Krishna M Karthik, Sayani Roy, Pallavi Bhyri
description: AimThis randomized, parallel-group study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of acupressure using the Aculief device compared to xylitol solution in minimizing pain perception during the delivery of local anesthesia (LA) in patients aged 6–9 years.MethodsFifty-four children were randomly allocated to either the Aculief group (n = 27) or the xylitol group (n = 27).

title: The extracellular vesicles of boar seminal plasma contain oxytocin at levels associated with fertility
creator: Ana Parra, Pablo Martínez-Díaz, María Botía, Marina López-Arjona, Xiomara Lucas, Isabel Barranco, Jordi Roca
description: Aim: Pig seminal plasma (SP) contains oxytocin (OXT) at levels associated with the fertility outcomes of boars used for artificial insemination (AI). However, OXT easily volatilizes when circulating freely, making it difficult to maintain stability in AI seminal doses. The hypothesis is that OXT is stably carried in seminal extracellular vesicles (EVs).

title: 178. Brain acidification in alcohol use disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis of postmortem pH
creator: H Hagihara, T Miyakawa
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAlcohol use disorder (AUD) not only severely diminishes patients' quality of life but also imposes substantial social burdens, with its prevalence growing worldwide in recent years. This underscores the urgent need to elucidate its underlying neural mechanisms.

title: 368. Relationship between childhood adversity and pre-operative structural MRI data in patients receiving deep brain stimulation of the subgenual cingulate cortex for treatment resistant depression
creator: E Ng, G Elias, J Germann, A Boutet, S Rizvi, A Lozano, S Kennedy, P Giacobbe
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAdverse childhood experiences (ACEs) predict poorer response to treatments for major depressive disorder (MDD) including medications, psychotherapy, and their combination. ACEs are known to have effects on brain structure and function.Aims & ObjectivesWe aim to characterize the relationship between ACE score and pre-operative structural MRI metrics in patients with treatment resistant depression (TRD) receiving deep brain stimulation (DBS) at the subgenual cingulate cortex (SCC).MethodThe ACE-10 questionnaire was used to quantify categories of ACEs.

title: Moringa oleifera leaf extract enhances rumen degradability and modifies methanogen communities in vitro
creator: Amr E. El-Nile, Marwa F. A. Attia, Mahmoud A. Elazab, Mohamed N. El-Gendy, Ahmed E. Kholif, Raed A. Aburawash, Elsayed E. Hafez, Sobhy M.A. Sallam
description: The development of innovative feed resources for livestock is crucial for ensuring nutrient adequacy while reducing greenhouse gas emissions. We aimed to evaluate the effects of Moringa oleifera leaf extract (ML) supplementation on in vitro nutrient degradability, net gas production (GP), ruminal fermentation, methane (CH4) emissions, and methanogen community structure using a semi-automated in vitro gas production system.

title: 582. Predicting psychiatric symptom deterioration using heart rate variability: the role of temporal feature engineering
creator: M K Kim, S Y Min, Y M Ahn
description: BackgroundPsychiatric care critically lacks objective biomarkers for monitoring symptom trajectories, often delaying the detection of clinical deterioration. While heart rate variability (HRV) offers promise as a continuous, non-invasive marker of autonomic function, prior prediction models have achieved only modest performance (AUC 0.55–0.65).

title: Comparative outcomes of prepectoral vs. subpectoral robot-assisted immediate prosthetic reconstruction following nipple-sparing mastectomy
creator: Hye Ju Han, Chang Jun Lee, Jun Yong Lee
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundRobot-assisted surgical techniques are increasingly adopted in breast reconstruction, yet the optimal implant placement approach remains debated. Robot-assisted nipple-sparing mastectomy (RANSM) with immediate prosthetic breast reconstruction using the Da Vinci system has shown improved cosmetic outcomes and patient satisfaction. While prepectoral reconstruction offers easier implant placement and fewer complications, subpectoral reconstruction provides better upper pole contours and reduced acellular dermal matrix (ADM) requirements.

title: 369. Integrating structured hospital-based psychosocial case management into national suicide prevention in South Korea: a multicentre, assessor-blinded, randomised controlled trial
creator: S M Lee, K-H Kim, M Baik, M-K Kim, P J Na, H-Y Lee, J W Paik
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSouth Korea maintains the highest suicide rate in the OECD despite ongoing prevention efforts. Major depressive disorder (MDD) is the leading diagnosis among suicide deaths, yet evidence for effective psychosocial interventions for suicidal ideation remains limited.Aims & ObjectivesThis study evaluated the effectiveness of a structured, hospital-based case management programme in reducing suicidal ideation and associated clinical outcomes among patients with MDD at suicidal risk.Method ​In this six-centre, assessor-blinded, randomised controlled trial, adults with MDD and current suicidal ideation or a recent attempt

title: Treasurer's Report for Financial Year 2024
creator: Aline Muyle
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). t account$1,999,912.54Prepaid expenses$129,790.00Accounts Receivable$127,991.88 Total Assets $3,069,458.87 LiabilitiesAccounts Payable$24,514.41Deferred Membership$29,883.29 Total Liabilities $54,397.70 Total Net Assets $3,015,061.17 Revenue overview SMBE's primary sources of revenue remain its 2 journals: Molecular Biology and Evolution (MBE): $529,157 Molecular Biology and Evolution (MBE): $529,157 Genome Biology and Evolution (GBE): $303,377 Genome Biology and Evolution (GBE): $303,377 In 2024, GBE revenue increased compared to 2023, while MBE revenue decreased.

title: 423. Suicidal symptoms as central nodes in late-life depression: a network analysis in older Koreans
creator: S Chang, T Y Choi
description: BackgroundLate-life depression is a major public health concern, particularly in rapidly aging societies such as South Korea, where suicide rates among older adults are among the highest in OECD countries. While network analysis has provided symptom-level insights into depressive disorders, few studies have examined DSM-based depressive symptom networks in older Asian populations using diagnostic interview data.

title: 204. Targeting the noradrenergic-metabolic axis: a new tailored therapeutic strategy for sugar-induced depression subtypes
creator: T Sakata, K Kunisawa, M Hasegawa, Y Seto, A Ogawa, H Kurahashi, Y Yamamoto, M Takemura, H Matsunami, T Sugai, N Kutsumura, K Saito, T Nabeshima, A Mouri
description: BackgroundMajor depressive disorder (MDD) has a highly heterogeneous pathophysiology. To optimize outcomes, it is necessary to identify clinically meaningful subtypes and provide treatments tailored to individual patients. Dietary habits have recently emerged as important modifiers of depression risk and treatment response. However, whether dietary habits influence the pathophysiology of MDD remains unclear.

title: Health diplomacy training, pedagogical approaches, and skills assessment: a scoping review
creator: Ashish Joshi, Laura Magana, Niharika Jha, Robert Otok, Ntuli Angyelile Kapologwe, Luís de Almeida Sampaio, Erica Kastrup, Woldekidan Amde, Rajendra Surenthirakumaran, Ayman El-Mohandes, Rodrigo Reis, So Yoon Kim, Catherine Kane, Tim K. Mackey, William Yotive, Henrique Barros, Ramune Kaledine, Josep
description: BackgroundHealth diplomacy is gaining increasing importance as an approach in addressing domestic and global health challenges, yet educational programs that prepare future practitioners remain underdeveloped in addressing skills core to this domain of public health practice. Training in health diplomacy is critical for building interdisciplinary competencies needed to navigate increasingly complex negotiations, cross-cultural engagements, and policy influence.

title: A transcriptomic atlas at bulk and single-cell levels identifies novel transcriptional and splicing regulators of ECM homeostasis in osteoarthritis
creator: Xiguang Ye, Chunyan Zheng, Hao Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common chronic degenerative joint disease. Chondrocytes undergo dynamic changes during the pathogenesis of OA, and the destruction of the extracellular matrix (ECM) and its homeostatic disruption are hallmarks of OA. This study explores the roles of transcriptional and alternative splicing (AS) mechanisms in regulating extracellular matrix (ECM) homeostasis in osteoarthritis (OA), using bulk and single-cell RNA-sequencing data.

title: 200. Psychotropic use, initiation, and healthcare trajectories in the 180 days before suicide
creator: Y-S Li, S-J Tsai, C-M Cheng, Y-M Bai, T-J Chen, M-H Chen
description: BackgroundSuicide is a major public health challenge globally and the tenth leading cause of death in Taiwan. Although psychiatric disorders, emergency visits, and psychotropic prescribing are known correlates of suicide, evidence from Asian populations remains limited—particularly regarding the timing, continuity, and clinical context of psychiatric versus non-psychiatric care preceding death.

title: 357. Transcranial magnetic stimulation in borderline personality disorder: results of a randomized sham-controlled study
creator: L Ustohal, M Horký, P Bartys, M Jáni, K Rektorová, M Radimecká, M Lamoš, M Vereš, T Brabec, P Horká Linhartová
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundBorderline personality disorder (BPD) is a devastating pervasive mental disorder characterized by emotion regulation impairment and marked impulsive behavior, including self-harming and suicidal behavior. Among other treatment possibilities in BPD, repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has been repeatedly used with inconclusive results because of protocols heterogeneity, lack of randomized controlled trials and poor quality of included studies, including high risk of methodological biases (Lisoni et al., 2022; Mansour et al., 2025).Aims & ObjectivesThe aim of the project was to assess the efficacy

title: 409. Epigenetic signatures of adolescent depression: unraveling the role of parental maltreatment
